s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with purulent discharge
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Purulent discharge for 10 months
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI
Opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of right upper eyelid swelling
10 months of purulent discharge
No history of trauma to the head
No symptoms of fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Node measures 11 × 7 mm
MRI shows high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
CT shows opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses
Expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses without bone destruction
Histopathology reveals mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Opacification and expansion of sinuses on CT, and high signal on T2-weighted MRI

shortlist.label: orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purulent discharge and immovable scarlike node on the eyelid

shortlist.label: caruncular abscess due to actinomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic purulent discharge and absence of trauma history

shortlist.label: tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic inflammation and presence of lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate on histopathology

shortlist.label: granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate on histopathology

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a long-standing, immovable, scarlike node on the right upper eyelid with purulent discharge, along with imaging findings of sinus opacification and expansion without bone destruction, and histopathology showing mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, is most consistent with actinomycosis, which is known for forming chronic, indolent infections with sinus tract formation and discharge.

rejected.label: sinusitis
rejected.why: While the patient has opacification of the sinuses, the primary issue is the chronic, localized infection of the eyelid, which is not typical for sinusitis alone.

rejected.label: orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: The lack of symptoms such as fever, headache, or significant nasal discharge, and the chronic nature of the condition, make acute orbital cellulitis less likely.

rejected.label: tuberculosis
rejected.why: There's no specific evidence provided in the case that would strongly suggest tuberculosis, such as systemic symptoms, known exposure, or histopathological findings typical of TB.

rejected.label: granulomatosis
rejected.why: The histopathological findings do not specifically indicate granulomatous disease, and the clinical presentation does not align closely with granulomatosis with polyangiitis or other granulomatous conditions.
